observations.contract: Pickup local anchor and world frame
observations.trace: Current client WorldGrabTargets applies GlobalTransform.transform_point(-physical.anchor_offset_m) before range and terrain visibility selection; fallback visual similarly uses local -anchor_offset below its item placeholder. Current authoritative server pickup uses item_box_center(item_transform.translation, physical), subtracting without rotation, while drop attaches that local offset to a dynamic compound collider. The already recorded REVIEW-PICKUP-ANCHOR-WORLD-PROJECTION-001 and earlier ADLER-L11-PICKUP-ANCHOR-FRAME own the conditional frame issue.
observations.remaining: Reuse the existing connected repair entry, not a second issue; actual rotated pose, derived catalog values, scale, client/server timing and exact aliases stay open.

observations.contract: Generated belt sockets and rig frame
observations.trace: Current garment_sockets calculates world socket poses from generated garment points and reparents them to the body joint named RigJointName::ROOT. BoneRole::Pelvis maps to that same ROOT; current equipment_location_bone maps the four belt locations to Pelvis. The authored belt worn placement occupies those four locations and its attachment points list those belt locations. Runtime generation installs the resulting sockets on the item. This supports the intended producer/consumer frame for that source-level belt path.
observations.remaining: It does not prove actual asset content, fit completion, non-belt/custom ancestry, all valid topology permutations or an observed correct pose. Server transfer rejects moving an item with children in the inspected slot path, but other producers and lifecycle states remain open.

observations.trace: Historical equipment.rs schedules an egui slot HUD. Current equipment.rs schedules slot_hud::push_slot_hud, which builds serialized views and calls hud::view. The 95e bridge calls browser window functions for wasm and is a no-op on native; the 95e crate README explicitly documents that the native client has no HUD and the justfile describes native performance playtesting. Both current supported browser hosts install the page HUD before boot.
observations.remaining: This records an explicitly documented native/browser behavior difference, not an assumed regression or instruction to restore an old HUD. Whether the native playtesting policy satisfies every desired use and all input/legibility requirements is a separate open product-policy question; no browser or native client was run.

observations.trace: Both historical and current icon paths check recipe size, generator version, decode and design hash before a warm cache lookup; separate weapon and holder source variants distinguish keys. Current generated icon pages send RGBA bytes via hud::icon before caching the page key, and the JS handler copies the wasm bytes to a canvas and retains its data URL. Both normal hosts install the handler before runtime boot.
observations.remaining: No image, canvas, asset fetch, renderer, cache lifecycle or browser result was observed. Other host/reload/error policy and all generator error owners remain open; earlier ADLER-L11-FORGE-GENERATION-CAUSE-DISCARD is not silently cleared.

observations.contract: Physical proxy change and fallback lifecycle
observations.trace: spawn_item_placeholders uses Added<TacticalEquipmentPhysical> and change filters for topology, properties and appearances, but no Changed<TacticalEquipmentPhysical>. Its fallback Cuboid dimensions and local anchor are built at spawn. The inspected normal player projection initially inserts the proxy; the 95e exact-name source search did not reveal an ordinary in-place physical writer.
observations.remaining: If an admitted in-place physical change can occur without any other selected trigger, existing fallback geometry could remain stale. Producer reachability, mutation policy, replication and actual invalidation remain unresolved, so this is an open conditional question rather than a proven defect or an instruction to add a trigger.
